_comment: The svGolf site generator's configuration (site/build.py). Paths are repository paths as inside lean-surfaces: `svgolf/...` is svGolf's own tree, anything else is lean-surfaces' (site/build.py's `repo_file`, in either layout). `tasks`: every task directory's listing (tutorial | listed | preview | hidden; a task missing here is hidden, with a warning; a preview is listed with its status line, content/tasks/<t>.json `preview_note`, and nothing of it is ranked: no par, no record, no board). `reference_player`: the player whose records are the proved references; they are par, the bar to beat, never ranked among the players. `pages`: which document each page renders; `omit`: the sections (by heading text, any level) left out of a document; `redact`: exact phrases replaced before rendering, in order (each must occur exactly once, or with `"all": true` at least once, every occurrence replaced; else the build fails as stale). `link_map`: where a Markdown link to a repository file goes on the site (task READMEs and Spec.lean files are mapped automatically); any other repository path is shown as unlinked text until `repo_url` (the public repository, not decided yet) is set. `repo_url`: null until the repository is public; while it is null, every task's "How to submit" says that public submissions open when the repository is published and shows the local flow only, and with a URL it shows the clone and the pull request. `denylist`: what must not appear in the output (checked case-insensitively); a hit fails the build. It is empty here: the markers of what is internal are not written in the repository, and `build.py --denylist FILE` adds them from a file kept outside it. A plain string must occur nowhere, the repository files offered byte for byte included. An object {"text", "scope": "site-text", "why", "allow"} is an internal marker (a maintainer's name, a work-package code, a review round, a tool used during development): it must not occur in the site's own text, which leaves out the repository files offered byte for byte (downloads and the `<pre data-src>` blocks that reproduce a file) and what players wrote in their records; `allow` names the pages where it is still expected, each with the reason (a page that no longer contains it fails the build as stale).

reproduce.description: How to reproduce an svGolf score bit for bit: the pinned tools and files with their hashes, the flow step by step, the commands.

proving.description: How to prove that a circuit meets an svGolf task's statement, with the sv_comb tactics.
